correctness.rationale: Conditioning on any fixed set of designated source vertices, all map images independently avoid that set; the map on its complement is uniform; this proves factorial cycle-vector deletion. First moments then give the finite covariance, product monotonicity gives exact signs. The factorwise product ratio yields a Gaussian mesoscopic profile; a telescoping Gaussian domination justifies both Riemann-summed limits. Direct enumeration of all maps through seven vertices checks exact identities, not the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Source vertices are a natural feed-in population; directed cycles are the feedback core. The exact all-cycle-length sign profile separates uncorrelated self-loops from strictly negatively associated longer cycles, while the square-root mesoscopic density determines two nontrivial aggregate correction limits. These are interpretable structural finite-size dependence laws, not an arbitrary small parameter table.
